references.text: The term 'azkara' (memorial offering/remembrance offering) is also used here, describing the portion of the grain offering that is burned on the altar as a fire offering to the Lord.
The priest shall take the memorial portion of the grain offering and burn it on the altar as a fire offering with a pleasing aroma to the Lord.
The priest shall burn the memorial portion on the altar as a fire offering to the Lord, using the same terminology and practice.
Describes how the priest is to lift up a handful of the fine flour from the grain offering mixed with oil and all the frankincense, and burn the memorial offering on the altar.
Frankincense is placed on the breads as a memorial offering, a fire offering to the Lord - the same concept involving frankincense and memorial offerings.
The priest shall burn the memorial portion on the altar as a fire offering to the Lord.
The atonement money shall serve as an 'azkara' (remembrance) for the people of Israel before the Lord.
